sentences.text: On the quiet planet of Tiny Rock, two friends named Podo and Didi spent their evenings watching the universe.
Between the two, Didi was always searching for excitement.
Suddenly, an amazing rainbow cloud floated near their rock.
It was a swirling cloud of stardust, glowing with vibrant shades of violet, orange, and emerald green.
"It is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen!" exclaimed Didi.
"I must have it.
I will capture a piece to keep on my shelf."
Podo frowned gently.
"I do not think you can own a cloud, Didi," he warned.
"Its beauty comes from its movement."
Ignoring his friend, Didi grabbed a net and caught a portion of the cloud in a clear crystal box.
"Got it!" he shouted triumphantly.
He rushed inside to display his treasure.
But as he set the box down, the vibrant light began to dim.
The swirling colors stopped moving.
The captured cloud transformed before their eyes.
It became a lifeless, dark gray clump of moisture, looking like a dirty raincloud.
"This is terrible," Didi groaned, tapping the glass.
"It looks like smoke.
Where did the magic go?"
"The magic was in the freedom," Podo said wisely.
"By trapping it, you extinguished its light.
Its light died when it cannot move."
Didi realized his mistake.
He looked at the dull box and then at the vast, open sky.
He picked up the box and ran back outside.
With a hopeful heart, Didi opened the crystal box.
The gray puff floated slowly out into the sky.
Instantly, the open sky brought it back to life.
The gray turned back to brilliant violet, orange, and emerald.
It joined the rest of the cloud, swirling happily.
"It is a masterpiece again," Didi whispered, watching it drift away.
"Indeed," agreed Podo.
"And now it is where it belongs.
That is the most beautiful thing of all."
They watched it fly freely and smiled.

principles: Story Grammar structures what is assessed but is not treated as the sole model of reading comprehension.
Scores reflect evidence of Story Element and relationship understanding, not lexical or semantic similarity alone.
100/67/33/0 are operational reporting values; they are not empirically calibrated IRT ability estimates.
Overall feedback must be combined with the lowest skill profile and selected misconception.
